mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES continues to trend upward from its recent low while TRANSIT also stabilizes, weekday foot traffic should recover and lift RETAIL_REC over the next 4 weeks. The mechanism fails if workplace and transit mobility do not translate into retail visits within one month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains at or below its last-4-week mean even after WORKPLACES rises by at least 3 points and TRANSIT rises by at least 2 points for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility is elevated, people spend more time at home and make fewer discretionary shopping trips, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the next 2 weeks. The signal is falsified if high residential staying-home does not coincide with weaker retail mobility soon after.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above 8 for two straight weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days despite RESIDENTIAL remaining above 8 and not falling by more than 1 point week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp recovery in TRANSIT combined with a concurrent lift in WORKPLACES indicates eased constraints on commuting and downtown access, which should raise RETAIL_REC over the next 4 weeks. The interaction matters because either series alone can move without generating shopping demand.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve over 28 days when TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both increase for at least two weeks in a row.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in PARKS mobility signals favorable outdoor weather and broader weekend activity, which should spill over into nearby retail visits within 1 week. The hypothesis fails if parks activity rises without any immediate retail lift.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by more than 8 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its prior-week value in the week after PARKS rises by more than 8 points.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM weakens while WORKPLACES is still below baseline, households are substituting toward essential errands and away from discretionary shopping, so RETAIL_REC should remain lower over the next 2 weeks. The claim fails if retail activity rebounds despite weak workplace mobility and soft essential-shopping mobility.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -14 while WORKPLACES stays below -15
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days even though GROCERY_PHARM stays below -14 and WORKPLACES stays below -15.

mechanism_narrative: A TRANSIT recovery above the recent low, without a matching rise in WORKPLACES, implies mobility is resuming for non-work trips only weakly; that pattern should leave RETAIL_REC flat to lower over the next 4 weeks. The mechanism fails if transit gains are broad enough to pull retail footfall higher.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -20 while WORKPLACES remains below -15
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC improves over 28 days even though TRANSIT rises above -20 and WORKPLACES stays below -15.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS and RESIDENTIAL both rise together, households are concentrating on local and home-based activity, which crowds out shopping trips and pushes RETAIL_REC downward over the next 1 to 2 weeks. The mechanism fails if local leisure and home-stay patterns coexist with stronger retail mobility.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises within 14 days while PARKS and RESIDENTIAL both remain above their prior-week levels.

mechanism_narrative: In a stable holiday- or event-driven week, a strong PARKS print followed by a lagged TRANSIT pickup should translate into higher retail activity with a 4-week delay. The lag matters because outdoor and transport activity often precede shopping trips by several days to weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -25 and TRANSIT turns upward the following week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-4-week average over the next 28 days after PARKS rises above -25 and TRANSIT turns up the next week.
